mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a multigenerational tiny home and a traditional accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: While a multigenerational tiny home can function as an ADU, the key difference lies in its specific design intent. A multigenerational tiny home is purpose-built to accommodate the distinct needs of multiple generations cohabiting, often featuring specialized layouts for shared yet private spaces. A traditional ADU is simply a secondary dwelling unit on a property, which may or may not be designed with multigenerational living in mind. Our multigenerational designs prioritize family dynamics and flexible living arrangements.
acceptedAnswer.description: A multigenerational tiny home is specifically designed for multiple generations, prioritizing shared yet private spaces, whereas an ADU is a general secondary dwelling.
